input:
Earlier scenes:
神农和他的家人住在古代，所以不知道什么植物能吃。因为他的家人常常生病了，所以神农和他的哥哥一起去旅行找可以吃的植物。他们去很多不一样的地方，比方说高山、山谷和沙漠。他们在很漂亮的河找夹竹桃。神农问他的哥哥：“我应该吃这种植物吗？”哥哥说：“这就要看你想要安全还是接近知道了。“神农一吃夹竹桃就生病了。哥哥说：“太麻烦了。

This scene:
夹竹桃是毒的，我想知道灵芝会帮他。”哥哥给神农灵芝。神农吃完了以后开始痊愈了。神农说：“谢谢哥哥，你帮得真好。灵芝我们可以吃，特别是如果我们已经吃了夹竹桃。“

The teacher's corrections on this scene (student words：her correction, her note):
- 夹竹桃是毒的：有毒的
- 我想知道灵芝会帮他：灵芝有没有用/能不能帮他
- 哥哥给神农灵芝：给了，了completed
- 你帮得真好：你做得很好

The system's feedback items:
1. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 夹竹桃是毒的：夹竹桃是有毒的，Use 有毒 as the adjectival description of a poisonous plant; 毒 alone does not fit this predicate pattern. [vocab list]
2. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 灵芝会帮他：灵芝会不会帮他，After 想知道, use a yes-or-no form such as 会不会 when the speaker is wondering whether something will happen. [rule: none]
3. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 夹竹桃。“：夹竹桃。”，The final quotation needs a closing quotation mark after the sentence-final punctuation. [rule: none]
4. [Grammar & Vocabulary, error] 开始痊愈了：开始好起来了，痊愈 describes being fully recovered, so it does not fit naturally after 开始; 好起来 describes the beginning of improvement. [rule: none]
5. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 我：神农，The narration has used third person, so 我 has no clearly established speaker here; repeat the name to identify whose thought this is. [rule: ambiguous_reference]
6. [Coherence: reference, error] Coherence (Reference): 他：自己，After 神农 becomes the subject of the thought, use 自己 to make clear that the lingzhi may help Shen Nong rather than his brother. [rule: ambiguous_reference]
7. [Coherence: temporality, error] Coherence (Temporality): 哥哥给神农灵芝：哥哥给了神农灵芝，Giving the lingzhi is a completed action in the event sequence, so the verb needs 了. [rule: aspect_le_completed]

items.reason: 毒 cannot directly serve as the adjectival predicate here; 有毒的 is correct.
After 想知道, a yes-or-no form such as 会不会 is appropriate, and the correction is grammatical.
The final quotation mark is the wrong type and should be a closing mark (”).
开始痊愈了 is somewhat less common than 开始好起来了 but is still acceptable Chinese.
我 can be the speaker of the direct speech or thought, so replacing it with 神农 is not required.
他 is acceptable here, as shown by the teacher's own alternative 能不能帮他.
The giving is a completed narrative event, so 给 needs 了.
